perspective:
Sara Manuelito’s available information is limited to what she personally experienced, observed, did, said, or heard:

- She knows she is an American Indian woman and a Speech-Language Pathologist. She knows Shirley Whiteplume is a nurse and a long-time colleague/close friend from their community health center, with whom she has worked for several years.
- She attended the funeral of a mutual patient. She observed Shirley appearing somber and suspected Shirley was deeply affected by the loss.
- At the funeral, Sara told Shirley she knew it must be hard and that she had seen how much Shirley cared. Shirley told her it had been tough and that she kept thinking if more could have been done. Sara replied they did everything they could and should remember the good care and joy they brought. Shirley said Sara was right but it was hard to let go.
- During a work coffee break, Sara raised the patient’s treatment decisions, sensing Shirley felt burdened by the outcome. Shirley said she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have improved his chance. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had and that the burden was too heavy to carry alone. Shirley appreciated this but said it was hard to accept.
- Sara observed Shirley remaining reserved and showing minimal emotion. During a quiet office moment, Sara confronted her, saying she noticed Shirley holding back feelings and that it was okay to be open. Shirley said she wasn’t sure she could and didn’t want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said showing emotion doesn’t make her weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley said Sara might be right and she would try to be more open.
- Sara later felt her confrontation may have been too harsh. She apologized to Shirley for coming on too strong. Shirley said it had been a bit much but she knew Sara meant well and appreciated the apology. Sara said she was there for Shirley however needed. Shirley thanked her and said they should keep talking because it helps.
- After some time, Sara noticed Shirley seemed improved, felt hopeful, and asked how she was. Shirley said she was feeling better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara suggested spending more time together outside work. Shirley agreed and suggested planning something for the weekend.

Sara does not have access to Shirley’s private thoughts, feelings, or background beyond what Shirley said or Sara could observe/participate in.
